title: Failed shadow rollout: drift analysis, auto-rollback rules, and runbook updates
creator: Lena Park
description:
Summary:
During a routine shadow rollout of model variant r2-2026-02, we observed a progressive quality regression on a subset of production traffic mirrored to shadow workers. The automated safety system did not trigger rollback because the configured gates monitored infra errors (5xx) and P50 latency only; quality regressions (semantic error / hallucination rate on our eval prompts) were not part of the gate.

Why this ticket exists:
This ticket collects the analysis, decisions and concrete follow-ups after the incident on 2026-02-18 where shadow traffic exhibited a 3x increase in 'hallucination' score on the internal eval set and a 2.1x increase in P95 latency on shadow pods. We need to (a) close gaps in our rollout gating, (b) update the runbook/playbooks for shadow deployments, (c) add isolation controls for shadow traffic, and (d) define robust auto-rollback heuristics that include quality signals.

Timeline (short):
- 2026-02-18 03:12 UTC: Canary deploy started for r2-2026-02; ~0.5% of production traffic mirrored to shadow.
- 2026-02-18 03:38 UTC: Ops alert — internal eval-run (periodic) shows hallucination metric jump from baseline 0.6% to 1.9% (rolling 30m).
- 2026-02-18 03:45 UTC: Latency dashboard: shadow P95 moved from 190ms baseline to 420ms.
- 2026-02-18 04:05 UTC: No infra-level errors observed; auto-rollback rules did not fire. Traffic mirroring paused manually at 04:11 UTC.

Observed data and signals:
- Quality delta (internal eval prompts): baseline 0.6% -> 1.9% (3.2x).
- Human-rated regressions (spot sample of 240 requests): 15% regression severity (confidently wrong answers).
- Latency: shadow P95 190ms -> 420ms, P50 85ms -> 130ms.
- Error rate (5xx): remained low (0.02% -> 0.03%).
- KV cache behavior: cache hit rate on shadow workers dropped by ~22%; memory pressure on shadow worker processes increased.

Root-cause hypotheses (ranked):
1) Model variant memory pattern + routing mismatch: r2-2026-02 uses slightly different tokenization (padding differences) interacting badly with our shared KV cache eviction heuristic when shadow traffic uses same cache namespace. Cache pollution led to worse latency and degraded context for longer conversations.
2) Shadow traffic distribution skew: mirrored traffic included a larger-than-expected proportion of long-sequence requests (by conf of route), amplifying cache pressure and P95.
3) Hidden micro-batch/prefill path differences in the runtime for shadow workers triggered a cold-path execution that increased token-level mishandling for certain prompt classes.

Why auto-rollback didn't trigger:
- Rollback gates only evaluated infra signals (5xx, CPU/GPU OOM, steady-up-latency) and not semantic/quality signals.
- Our shadow mirror rate (0.5%) created sparse but noisy quality signal; the rolling-window threshold was too narrow and averaged down the spike.

Actionable decisions (approved in review):
- Add a quality gate to rollout heuristics that includes a rolling eval-run result and a lightweight classification-based hallucination proxy. Gate fires if quality delta > 1.5x baseline for 30m and at least 200 matched prompt samples.
- Isolate KV cache per rollout namespace for shadow/canary workers to prevent cross-variant pollution.
- Limit shadow traffic to 0.2% by default for new model variants until a warm-up window of 6h of stable metrics is achieved.
- Add a latency-adjusted weight: if P95(shadow) > 2x baseline for 10m, trigger pause of mirroring and page on-call.
- Update runbook with explicit decision tree for shadow vs canary action (manual vs automatic).

- Evaluation harness run (raw): https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/eval-runs/2026-02-18-shadow-r2-2026-02.csv
- Dashboards: https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/rollout/shadow-r2-2026-02

remediation_actions: Deploy PR #4821 to isolate KV cache namespaces for rollouts (runtime change).
Ship rollout service change (PR #311) that adds eval-run and hallucination-proxy into gate checks and exposes gate thresholds in Console per project.
Lower default shadow mirror rate to 0.2% and add a 6h warm-up period flag per variant in the rollout config.
Add automated pause rule: if shadow P95 > 2x baseline for 10m -> pause mirroring + run automated sample extraction + page SRE.
Augment periodic eval-run to include stratified samples to reach 200 prompt matches within 30m windows (fallback to classifier when sample count low).
Update runbook: new decision tree, checklist for manual investigation, and links to dashboards and triage playbooks.
Create a lightweight smoke-suite that runs on every shadow worker instantiation to detect tokenization/serialization mismatches.
postmortem_findings: Missing quality signals in rollout automation allowed a semantic regression to persist without auto-rollback.
Shared KV cache namespace allowed cross-variant pollution; isolation reduces tail latency risk.
Shadow traffic composition differed from assumed distribution; we need traffic shape checks before mirroring full production subset.
Existing rolling-window thresholds diluted the signal; minimum sample counts must be enforced for quality gates.
experiments_planned: A/B: compare isolated KV cache (namespace per variant) vs shared cache on tail latency and cache-hit ratio for long-sequence traffic.
Experiment different mirror rates (0.1%, 0.2%, 0.5%) with warm-up gating to measure trade-off between detection speed and signal noise.
Shadow-only smoke-tests on boot that validate tokenization and prefilling edges using 30 synthetic prompts.
acceptance_criteria: Quality gate added to rollout service and visible in Console with editable thresholds.
KV cache namespace isolation deployed to rollout runtime and validated in staging with long-sequence synthetic load.
Default mirror rate lowered and warm-up period implemented; rollout metrics reflect stable behavior for 6h before automated increased mirroring.
Runbook updated and reviewed by on-call SRE and PM; tabletop exercise completed with SRE/Platform/Runtime teams.
